title: Cambodia’s NGO Sector Is Collapsing. Does It Matter?
gist: Cambodia's once-prolific NGO sector, with up to 6,100 registered groups, has been dismantled since the 2013 elections by the ruling CPP via the 2015 NGO law, tax audits, lawsuits and political pressure.

insights.claim: Cambodia hosted up to 6,100 registered NGOs and associations (about 3,450 NGOs), among the highest per capita in the world after Rwanda, before the sector's decline.
insights.speaker: Louise Coventry
insights.so_what: Sizeable aid-dependent civil society is being removed from a country long reliant on donor flows.

insights.claim: After the 2013 elections posed a major electoral threat, the CPP began dismantling the public sphere, viewing NGOs as vehicles for foreign-backed color revolutions, and used the 2015 Law on Associations and NGOs, tax audits, lawsuits and meeting disruption to restrict them.
insights.speaker: Louise Coventry
insights.so_what: Authoritarian consolidation in Cambodia is entrenched; expect continued donor-relations friction.
